summary: Sumi Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA under Alexander Leonhard Mayer at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and a PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr. at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Sumit Ganguly works in Indology. He held the Rabindranath Tagore Chair and directed the India Studies Program at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus (attested 2026), and is a Senior Fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution (attested 2026).

Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at the University of London (~1928–1931). He taught at Sir Parashurambhau College (~1937–1939), held a chair at Deccan College (1942–1971), and retired from UT Austin (~1971–1976).

Sun-Ah Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying with teachers Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.
Sunanda Mukhopadhyay works in linguistics and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and is a Research Scholar/Fellow at the Asiatic Society (both attested 2026).

Sung Bae Park (1934–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctorate under Lewis R. Lancaster. He taught at Dongguk University and became Professor Emeritus at Stony Brook University, which he joined in 1977.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen in 2001. Ahn served as Director at Geumgang University and as Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).

Sungtaek Cho (1957–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Cho held posts at Stony Brook University and Korea University, serving as Director at Korea University in 2003 and as Professor there (attested 2017).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under doctoral supervisor Phillip B. Zarrilli (attested 2013).

Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was an Indian linguist and Indologist. Educated at Scottish Church College, Presidency College, Calcutta, London, and Paris, he served as Khaira Professor at the University of Calcutta (1922–1952) and Government of India National Professor (~1965–1977).
Supree Kanjanapisarn works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Assumption University under doctoral supervisor Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2011).

Surama Dasgupta (1907–1988) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earning degrees from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge (PhD, 1948). She served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Calcutta and Cambridge (PhD ~1920–1922). He held posts at Chittagong College, Presidency College, Cambridge, Sanskrit College (Principal ~1931–1942), and the University of Calcutta (Chair of Philosophy ~1942–1945).

Surya Das (1950–) is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University at Buffalo (~1968–1971) and trained under traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1980–1999).

Suryakumar Bhuyan (1892–1964) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency College, Calcutta, and SOAS (PhD 1936). He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University.
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under teachers including Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, and James W. Benson.
Susan L. Beningson works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist Jr. (attested 2009).
Susan L. Huntington (1943–) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1972 to 2012.
